_README: Single-sample / statistical-threshold-value criteria for recreational
water, in counts per 100 mL. wq/fit.py reads this file; no threshold is
hardcoded anywhere in the code, and a lookup that finds no entry is
reported as 'no criterion' rather than silently defaulting to a number.
Lookup key is (state, analyte, water_class). water_class is 'fresh' for
Great Lakes sites and 'marine' everywhere else, because the enterococci
criterion genuinely differs between them. A state with no entry falls
back to '_default', and every fitted row records which entry it used in
its threshold_source column, so a result computed against the federal
fallback is never mistaken for one computed against a state's own rule.
EVERY ENTRY HERE CARRIES _verified: false. The values are transcribed
from the cited documents but were NOT checked against the live
regulation when this file was written, because outbound network access
was blocked in that session. Before publishing a result, re-read each
cited criterion, correct the number, and flip _verified. State beach
programs also change criteria; a 2012-RWQC state and a 1986-criteria
state will not agree, and that difference lands directly in the
exceedance-separation column.
CFU and MPN are different estimators and are NOT interconvertible. The
criteria below are written in whichever unit the source states; the
pipeline compares a count to them without rescaling, and records the
sample's own unit alongside, so a CFU/MPN mismatch stays visible.

_default._source: US EPA, 2012 Recreational Water Quality Criteria, EPA-820-F-12-058. Statistical Threshold Value (STV) at the 36/1000 illness rate, and the optional precautionary Beach Action Value (BAV) used by many state beach programs for a single-sample posting decision.

ECOLI.basis: 2012 RWQC STV, published for fresh water; applied to marine only as a fallback and flagged

FECAL.basis: EPA 1976 Quality Criteria for Water, fecal coliform single-sample bathing limit. Superseded federally but still in several state codes.

TOTAL.basis: total coliform bathing-water limit as used in state codes; no current federal criterion

ENT.basis: EPA 1986 Ambient Water Quality Criteria for Bacteria, EPA-440/5-84-002, freshwater enterococci single-sample maximum for a designated beach area

ECOLI.basis: EPA 1986 AWQC freshwater E. coli single-sample maximum for a designated beach area; also the 2012 RWQC BAV at the 36/1000 illness rate

FECAL.basis: EPA 1976 fecal coliform freshwater recreational limit

TOTAL.basis: state-code total coliform limit; no current federal criterion

CA._source: California Code of Regulations Title 17, sections 7957-7961 (AB 411), single-sample standards for ocean water contact sports areas. California also adopted the 2012 RWQC enterococci objectives into the Ocean Plan (2019); where the two differ, AB 411 is what a beach posting decision is made against, which is the decision this column is modelling.

ECOLI.basis: not an AB 411 ocean standard; carried from the freshwater criterion and flagged

TOTAL.basis: AB 411 single-sample standard. A second AB 411 rule drops this to 1,000 when the fecal-to-total ratio exceeds 0.1; that rule needs both analytes on the same sample and is NOT applied here — see wq/fit.py.

states._GREAT_LAKES_NOTE: Great Lakes states (MI, WI, IL, IN, OH, PA, NY, MN) are served by the _default fresh block: E. coli 235/100 mL, which is the 1986 single-sample maximum most Great Lakes beach programs post against. Add a state block here wherever the state's own criterion differs.
